scenarios.title: Ramadan Begins: {J} Plans His Month
scenarios.text: Sahur at 3:30am, training in the afternoon heat, matches kicking off around iftar. {J} grew up fasting through school football; doing it as a professional is a different kind of test. The club nutritionist has a plan ready if he wants it.
scenarios.prompt: How do you manage Ramadan this season?

choices.label: Fast with the club plan
choices.desc: Adjust sleep, meal timing and training load with the staff.
choices.text: The plan works: shorter, sharper sessions, dates and water on the touchline at iftar. {J} feels the month, but manages it.

choices.label: Fast and train as normal
choices.hint: Bigger fitness dip; character on show.
choices.text: The last ten days are hard. {J} finishes sessions grey-faced — and finishes them.

scenarios.title: Iftar With the Whole Squad
scenarios.text: The club organises an iftar dinner for the whole squad: Muslim and non-Muslim players, staff, families. Long tables, dates, kolak, a short prayer. The foreign players ask questions; the local players explain.

scenarios.title: The Supporter Groups Invite {J}
scenarios.text: The club's biggest supporter group invites {J} to their headquarters: a small building covered in murals, drums stacked in the corner, three generations of fans. They want him to sing the chants with them.

choices.label: Go and sing
choices.text: {J} sings every chant, badly, beating a drum out of time. The leaders laugh, then give him a scarf. Saturday, the whole stand sings his name.

choices.label: Politely decline
choices.text: {J} sends a signed shirt instead. The leaders are polite. The terrace is cooler.

scenarios.title: Away Fans Banned for the Big Derby
scenarios.text: The police ban away supporters from the derby after last season's violence. The away stand will be empty. The home crowd will be 40,000 people who hate {club}.
scenarios.prompt: The captain asks how you feel about it.

choices.label: “Good. More noise for us to silence.”
choices.text: Someone tells a journalist. The quote is printed on a rival banner. It's going to be a loud afternoon.

choices.label: “I hope everyone gets home safe.”
choices.text: The quote is shared by supporters of both clubs. A rare moment of peace.

scenarios.title: Kanjuruhan Remembered
scenarios.text: October. Before kick-off, the stadium falls silent for the 135 people who died at Kanjuruhan in 2022. Players link arms in the centre circle. Some supporters cry. Indonesian football still carries that night.

scenarios.title: Flares Stop the Match
scenarios.text: Twenty minutes in, flares rain onto the pitch from the home end. The referee takes the players off. Smoke drifts across the stadium. The club faces a fine, maybe a stadium ban.
scenarios.prompt: The supporters' leaders ask players to calm the crowd.

choices.label: Walk to the stand and appeal
choices.desc: Hands up, ask them to stop.
choices.hint: Could calm them. Could be ignored.

ok.text: {J} walks to the stand with his palms raised. The flares stop. The crowd chants his name instead.

bad.text: Nobody listens. Another flare lands near his feet. The match is abandoned.

choices.label: Stay in the tunnel
choices.text: The match restarts after forty minutes. The club is fined.

scenarios.title: Stuck in Mudik Traffic
scenarios.text: {J} tries to drive home for Lebaran like everyone else in Java. Eighteen hours in traffic on the toll road. People in other cars recognise him and wave. A family in a pickup truck passes him lontong through the window.

scenarios.title: 17 Agustus: {J} at the Village Games
scenarios.text: Independence Day. Every kampung holds games: sack races, climbing the greased pinang pole, krupuk-eating contests. {J}'s old neighbourhood invites him to judge. They want him to climb the pole.

out.text: Covered in grease, {J} reaches the prizes at the top and throws them down to the children. The video goes national.
He slips from halfway and lands on two uncles. Everyone laughs. His ankle is sore for a week.

choices.label: Judge only
choices.desc: Your club would want you to.
choices.text: {J} judges the krupuk contest with total seriousness. A seven-year-old wins.

scenarios.title: {J} Can't Find Food From Home
scenarios.text: Three months abroad and {J} would trade a goal for a plate of his mother's cooking. The supermarket has nothing he recognises. His weight is dropping.

choices.label: Learn to cook it yourself
choices.text: His mother teaches him over video, shouting instructions. The first attempt is terrible. The fifth is perfect. Teammates start asking for invitations.

choices.label: Adapt to local food
choices.text: {J} learns to love the local food. Mostly. He still dreams about sambal.

scenarios.title: Racist Abuse From the Stands
scenarios.text: During an away match, a group of home fans make monkey noises every time {J} touches the ball. The referee hears it. {M} hears it. The whole stadium hears it.

choices.label: Report it, follow protocol
choices.desc: The match stops; announcements are made.
choices.text: The match is stopped. An announcement. The fans are identified and banned for life. {J}'s teammates stand around him.

choices.label: Walk off the pitch
choices.hint: A statement the world will see.
choices.text: {J} walks off. His whole team follows. The match is abandoned. The story is everywhere, and the governing body is forced to act.

choices.label: Keep playing
choices.text: {J} keeps playing and scores the winner later, staring at the stand. It doesn't make the noises hurt less.

scenarios.title: {J} Gives His First Interview in the Local Language
scenarios.text: After months of lessons, {J} gives a post-match interview in the local language. Grammar mistakes, a strong accent, one wrong word that makes the reporter laugh. The fans love it.

scenarios.title: Hometown Holds a Parade for {J}
scenarios.text: {J}'s hometown wants to honour him: a parade, a ceremony at the town hall, a mural on the market wall. The mayor is very enthusiastic. Elections are next year.

choices.label: Attend gladly
choices.desc: For the people, not the mayor.
choices.text: The parade goes past his old school. Children run beside the car. His grandmother waves from her porch.

choices.label: Ask them to skip the politics
choices.desc: Only if there are no speeches.
choices.text: No speeches, just a football clinic in the town square. The mayor sulks. The children don't care.

scenarios.title: Rainy Season Chaos
scenarios.text: Rain every afternoon. The training pitch is a lake. The match on Saturday was postponed after the pitch flooded. The fixture list is now chaos.

scenarios.title: The Lucky Charm
scenarios.text: Before a big match, {J}'s grandmother sends a small amulet from a village shaman: “Wear it in your sock.” Some teammates laugh. Others quietly have their own.

choices.label: Wear it
choices.text: {J} plays with the amulet in his sock. He plays well. Coincidence. Probably.

choices.label: Keep it at home
choices.desc: Respect it, don't rely on it.
choices.text: The amulet stays on his bedside table.

scenarios.title: Umrah With His Parents
scenarios.text: {J}'s parents have dreamed their whole lives of going to Mecca for umrah. The off-season is long enough. The trip would cost {cost}.

choices.label: Go together
choices.text: Two weeks in Mecca and Medina with his parents. His father holds his hand at the Kaaba and can't speak. {J} comes back changed.

choices.label: Pay for them, stay and train
choices.text: {J} pays for his parents' umrah. They send photos every day.

scenarios.title: Holidays Alone Abroad
scenarios.text: The league pauses for the holidays. Teammates fly home to families. {J}'s flight home is too long for the break. He'll spend it in an empty apartment.

choices.label: Accept a teammate's invitation
choices.text: {T}'s grandmother feeds {J} until he can't move and gives him a knitted scarf. He's part of the family now.

choices.label: Fly home anyway
choices.desc: Thirty hours of travel for four days at home.
choices.text: Thirty hours of travel for four days at home. Worth every minute.

choices.label: Stay and rest
choices.text: {J} sleeps, trains alone in an empty gym, watches films. It's peaceful, and a bit sad.

scenarios.title: The Ultras Hear {J} Might Leave
scenarios.text: The supporters who adopted {J} have heard the transfer rumours. A banner appears at training: “LOYALTY OR NOTHING.” His name is painted under it, then crossed out, then painted again.

choices.label: Meet them
choices.text: {J} meets the leaders. They don't like what they hear, but they respect that he came.

choices.label: Say nothing
choices.text: Silence. The next match, his name isn't sung.

scenarios.title: Derby Week: The City Holds Its Breath
scenarios.text: Derby week. Every taxi driver, every street vendor, every old man at the mosque or the market has advice for {J}. His neighbours have painted their fence in the club colours.
scenarios.prompt: A rival fan corners you at a petrol station, friendly but intense.

choices.label: Banter back
choices.text: Five minutes of hilarious banter. The video makes both fanbases laugh.

choices.label: Smile, sign, leave
choices.text: {J} signs the man's arm, of all things. Rival or not.

scenarios.title: Three Hours to Training
scenarios.text: A protest, a flood and a broken-down truck at the same intersection. {J} has been in the car for three hours and training started forty minutes ago.

choices.label: Ojek!
choices.text: {J} abandons the car and jumps on an ojek. The driver realises who he is and drives like it's a cup final. He makes the end of training.

choices.label: Call {M} and apologise
choices.text: {M} sighs. Half the squad is stuck too.

scenarios.title: Earthquake Hits the Region
scenarios.text: An earthquake hits a region near the club's home. Hundreds of families have lost their houses. The club suspends training for two days. Several players drive to help.

choices.label: Drive there and help
choices.text: Two days of carrying rice sacks and building tents. Nobody films it, at {J}'s request. Somebody does anyway.

choices.label: Donate
choices.text: {J} donates quietly through a relief agency.

scenarios.title: The Naturalisation Debate Gets Personal
scenarios.text: On a talk show, a pundit argues that local players like {J} are being overlooked for the national team because of naturalised players from Europe. He uses {J} as his example. Nobody asked {J}.

choices.label: Support the naturalised players
choices.text: “We're all Garuda. Make the team better and we all win.” The national team staff notice.

choices.label: Agree with the pundit
choices.hint: Popular with some fans, unpopular with federation.
choices.text: The quote becomes a culture-war headline. Some fans love it. The national team coach doesn't call.

choices.label: Stay out of it
choices.text: {J} says nothing. His football does the arguing.

scenarios.title: Teaching a Dutch-Born Teammate Bahasa
scenarios.text: At national team camp, a newly naturalised player born in the Netherlands, {T}, asks {J} to teach him some Bahasa Indonesia for the anthem and the fans. He's nervous about pronouncing things wrong.

scenarios.title: Batik Day Photoshoot
scenarios.text: National Batik Day. The club asks every player to wear batik for a photoshoot. {J}'s mother sends a shirt she had made specially, in the pattern of their home region.

scenarios.title: Match Kicks Off Before Iftar
scenarios.text: Saturday's match kicks off at 4pm. Sunset is at 5:55pm. {J} will play most of the match while fasting, in the heat. The club doctor wants to discuss options.

choices.label: Keep fasting, break it at the break in play
choices.desc: The referee allows a short pause at sunset.
choices.text: At sunset, the referee pauses play for a minute. {J} drinks water and eats a date by the touchline. The crowd applauds.

choices.label: Make up the fast another day
choices.desc: Permitted for travellers and those with heavy work.
choices.text: {J} decides to make up the day later, after speaking with an ustaz. Full energy for the match.

scenarios.title: Exploring the New City
scenarios.text: {J} has lived here for months but only knows the route between his apartment and the training ground. A teammate offers to show him the city on their day off.

choices.label: Explore
choices.text: A day of markets, old streets and a strange local dessert. For the first time, the city feels like his.

choices.label: Rest at home
choices.text: {J} stays home and plays video games with friends back home.

scenarios.title: A Fan's Handmade Gift
scenarios.text: An elderly supporter waits at the training ground gate every day for a week. When {J} finally stops, she gives him a hand-painted portrait of him celebrating a goal, made over two months.

scenarios.title: The Pitch Where It All Started
scenarios.text: {J} visits the dusty field where he learned to play: a rice-paddy edge, two bamboo goalposts, a ball made of plastic bags. It's going to be sold to a developer.

choices.label: Buy the land
choices.desc: {cost}: a pitch for the village forever.
choices.text: {J} buys the land and builds a proper pitch with real goals. The village kids christen it with a match that lasts until dark.

choices.label: Let it go
choices.text: {J} takes a photo of the bamboo goalposts and lets it go.

scenarios.title: Team Bus Attacked Before an Away Match
scenarios.text: On the way to an away match, stones hit the team bus. A window shatters. Nobody is seriously hurt, but the players are shaken. The match is still on.

choices.label: Play — don't let them win
choices.text: The team plays with fury. {J} celebrates the goal in front of the home end with a finger to his lips.

choices.label: Support postponing
choices.text: The captain asks for postponement. The federation agrees. The match is replayed months later behind closed doors.

scenarios.title: {J} Learns the Wrong Words
scenarios.text: His teammates have been teaching {J} local slang. He confidently uses one phrase with the club president's wife. The squad is crying with laughter. The president's wife is not.

scenarios.title: Street Vendors Sell Fake {J} Shirts
scenarios.text: Outside the stadium, street vendors sell knock-off shirts with {J}'s name and number for a fraction of the official price. The club wants him to post a warning against fakes.

choices.label: Post it
choices.text: The post annoys fans who can't afford official shirts.

choices.label: Refuse
choices.desc: Not every fan can afford the real one.
choices.text: {J} refuses. The club is annoyed. The fans love him for it.

scenarios.title: {J} Sees Snow for the First Time
scenarios.text: {J} opens the curtains and the world is white. He has never seen snow. He runs outside in slippers, takes forty photos and a video for his mother, and makes the worst snowman in history.

scenarios.title: Team Karaoke Night
scenarios.text: Karaoke is mandatory after a big win. {M} sings a love song terribly and the squad films it. Now everyone is looking at {J}.

choices.label: A dangdut classic
choices.text: The whole squad, coaches included, dances. A dressing-room classic is born.

choices.label: A heartfelt ballad
choices.text: Silence, then applause. Someone is wiping their eyes and blaming the air conditioning.

scenarios.title: Hometown Gossip Turns Sour
scenarios.text: Back home, gossip has started: that {J} forgot where he came from, that his family has become arrogant, that he doesn't help anyone. His mother heard it at the market and came home upset.

choices.label: Do something visible at home
choices.text: A free football clinic for two hundred kids ends the gossip in one afternoon.

choices.label: Ignore it
choices.text: {J} ignores it. His mother doesn't go to that market any more.

scenarios.title: A Trip to Papua With a Teammate
scenarios.text: {T}, a teammate from Papua, invites {J} home for a week in the off-season: mountains, rivers, a village where every boy plays football barefoot on red earth, and many of them are better than {J} was at their age.

scenarios.title: Halal Food at the Club Canteen
scenarios.text: The club canteen doesn't label halal options clearly. {J} has been eating salads and rice for weeks to be safe. The nutritionist has noticed his protein intake is too low.

choices.label: Ask the club
choices.text: The club introduces clearly labelled halal options within a month. Three other players thank {J}.

choices.label: Bring your own food
choices.text: {J} meal-preps every Sunday. His lunchbox becomes famous in the dressing room.

scenarios.title: Lost in Translation at a Press Conference
scenarios.text: A translator mistranslates {J}'s answer at a press conference. He said he was “happy to be here”; the translation said he was “happy to be here for now”. The headline: “{J} HINTS AT EXIT.”

choices.label: Post a correction video
choices.text: His clumsy but sincere video in the local language wins the fans over completely.

choices.label: Ask the club to correct it
choices.text: The club issues a correction. Most fans believe it.

scenarios.title: New Year's Eve Before a Match
scenarios.text: New Year's Eve. The city is exploding with fireworks and parties. There's a match on the 2nd. Teammates are going out. {J}'s phone is full of invitations.

choices.label: Watch fireworks from the balcony, early night
choices.text: Fireworks from the balcony, a video call home at midnight, asleep by 12:30.

out.text: A brilliant night, home by 2am, feeling fine.
Photos from the club at 4am reach {M}'s phone.

scenarios.title: Forty-Five Degrees in the Gulf
scenarios.text: Training starts at 9pm because the day is too hot. {J} sleeps in the afternoon and lives at night. His body clock is completely broken.

scenarios.title: Visit to an Inner-City School
scenarios.text: The club's community programme sends {J} to a school in the poorest part of the city. The pitch is concrete. The goals have no nets. Three hundred children are waiting.

scenarios.title: Indonesia Raya Before Kick-Off
scenarios.text: Before every match in Indonesia, the national anthem plays. Today, a little girl in the mascot line sings it so loudly and so out of tune that the whole stadium joins in, laughing and singing. {J} sings with his hand on his heart, grinning.

scenarios.title: Fans Ride Twelve Hours to an Away Match
scenarios.text: Three hundred supporters travelled twelve hours by bus, motorbike and boat to an away match across the archipelago. After the final whistle they're still singing. {J} sees a boy of ten among them, asleep on his father's shoulders.

choices.label: Give them your shirt and boots
choices.text: {J} walks to the fence and hands his shirt to the boy, now awake and speechless. The supporters sing his name all the way home.

choices.label: Applaud them
choices.text: {J} applauds them with the team. They applaud back.
